<!-- Generated from the code by make docs-reference: do not edit. -->

Every action on a Cahut goes through a registry of operations. The MCP tools and the command line are thin layers over it: the registry checks who calls, runs the operation and writes the Logbook. Each Cahut has its own registry and its own Logbook, and so does the server that holds the Cahuts.

Each operation states who may call it: any person of the Cahut, its administrators, or the administrators of the server, who use the command line. An AI acts with the rights of the person it acts for.

## Operations of a Cahut

| Operation | What it does | Who calls it | Changes data | Offered to AIs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activate_account` | Choose a password from a single-use activation link, and sign in. | Anyone, to sign in | yes | no, people only |
| [`add_room_member`](/reference/mcp-tools/#add_room_member) | Add a person to a team Room, as a member or an owner. They can then open and publish its Windows. | Any person; nobody in an individual Cahut | yes | yes |
| `approve_authorization` | Connect an AI client to this Cahut, for the person who consents, with the scope and the Rooms they grant. Returns the address that sends the browser back to the client, with its authorization code. | Any person | yes | no, people only |
| `approve_knock` | Approve a Knock of one of your AIs: the call runs now, as the AI, and what it returns comes to you. It may still fail, if things changed since the AI called. | Any person | yes | no, people only |
| `change_email` | Change your e-mail address: a link goes to the new one, which replaces yours once you use the link, within 24 hours, and your old address gets a notice. An empty address removes yours at once. | Any person | yes | no, people only |
| `change_handle` | Change your handle, with which you sign in. Your personal Room takes it as its name: the addresses of its Windows change, the old ones stop working, and your old handle is free for another person or Room. In an individual Cahut, your other Rooms, whose names start with your handle, take the new one too. Answer the Knocks that wait for you first. | Any person | yes | no, people only |
| `change_name` | Change your name, as the people of the Cahut see it. Your personal Room takes it too, unless you gave it a title of its own. | Any person | yes | no, people only |
| `change_password` | Change your password. Your other sessions end. | Any person | yes | no, people only |
| `check_handle` | Say whether a handle can go to a new person: of the form of a handle, not reserved, and held by no person and by no Room. For the administrators of the Cahut. | Administrators of the Cahut | no | no, people only |
| `confirm_email` | Confirm a new e-mail address from the link sent to it, which makes it the address of its person. | Anyone, to sign in | yes | no, people only |
| `create_activation_link` | Give a person a new single-use link, valid 7 days, where they choose their password, for instance after they forgot it. It goes to their e-mail address too, when they have one and the Cahut sends e-mail. Their password works until they use the link. | Administrators of the Cahut | yes | no, people only |
| [`create_room`](/reference/mcp-tools/#create_room) | Create a team Room, at &lt;domain&gt;/&lt;name&gt;/. You become its owner, and can then add members. Windows published in it are for its members. In an individual Cahut, you stay its only member, and its name starts with your handle and a hyphen. | Any person | yes | yes |
| `create_service_token` | Create a service token, with which a program on this server manages the people of the Cahut through the admin API, without a Knock: it creates them, gives them their activation link, and disables them. | Administrators of the server | yes | no, people only |
| [`create_share_link`](/reference/mcp-tools/#create_share_link) | Make a share link: whoever holds it opens the Window, without an account or a Key, until it ends, besides its access. It ends in 7 days unless you give an end, 30 days at most, and may open to a number of readers only. It is returned this once: give it to the person. revoke_share_link takes it back. Not for a public Window. | Any person | yes | yes |
| `create_token` | Create a personal token that lets an AI act on behalf of a person. | Any person | yes | no, people only |
| [`create_user`](/reference/mcp-tools/#create_user) | Create a person, with their personal Room, and the link where they choose their password, which goes to their e-mail address when you give one and the Cahut sends e-mail. | Administrators of the Cahut | yes | to the AIs of administrators |
| [`delete_room`](/reference/mcp-tools/#delete_room) | Delete a team Room for good, with its members and its Windows, those in its trash included, and their files: this cannot be undone. | [`delete_user`](/reference/mcp-tools/#delete_user) | Delete a person for good: their account, their tokens and the AIs they connected, their personal Room and the team Rooms they are the only owner of, with the Windows of these Rooms and their files. This cannot be undone. The Windows they published in other Rooms stay, without an author. Their handle becomes free. No one deletes themself, nor the last administrator of the Cahut; disable_user stops a person and keeps what is theirs. | Administrators of the Cahut | yes | to the AIs of administrators |
| `deny_authorization` | Refuse the request of an AI client to connect to this Cahut. Returns the address that tells the client so. | Any person | yes | no, people only |
| `deny_knock` | Deny a Knock of one of your AIs: the call never runs. The AI learns it from get_knock. | Any person | yes | no, people only |
| `describe_authorization` | Check the request of an AI client to connect to this Cahut, and describe it to the person who consents: the client, where it will be sent back, the scope it asks for, and the Rooms the person may grant. | Any person | no | no, people only |

| `disconnect_ai` | Disconnect an AI connected over OAuth. Its tokens stop working at once; to use it again, the person connects it again. | Any person | yes | no, people only |
| `dismiss_report` | Decide a report that waits, and leave its Window as it is, with a note for the moderators. For the moderators of this Cahut. | Administrators of the Cahut | yes | no, people only |
| [`enable_user`](/reference/mcp-tools/#enable_user) | Enable a disabled person again: they can sign in, and their AIs can act with their tokens. | Administrators of the Cahut | yes | to the AIs of administrators |

| `get_invitation` | Describe the invitation of a personal link: the Window, who invites, and their note. | Anyone, to sign in | no | no, people only |
| [`get_knock`](/reference/mcp-tools/#get_knock) | Check a Knock of this Cahut, a call of an AI that waits for a person to approve it: whether it waits, was approved and run, failed, was denied, expired or was canceled. Call it to learn what became of a call that knocked. | Any person | no | yes |

## Operations of the server

They are not offered over MCP.

| Operation | What it does | Who calls it | Changes data | Offered to AIs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `activate_account` | Choose a password from a single-use activation link, as an administrator of the server, and sign in. | Anyone, to sign in | yes | no, people only |
| `add_domain` | Declare a domain on this server, which creates the Cahut at that domain, optionally with its first administrator and the link where they choose their password. | Administrators of the server | yes | no |
| `change_password` | Change your password, as an administrator of the server. Your other sessions end. | Administrators of the server | yes | no, people only |
| `create_activation_link` | Give an administrator of the server a new single-use link, valid 7 days, where they choose their password, for instance after they forgot it. Their password works until they use the link. | Administrators of the server | yes | no, people only |
| `create_admin` | Create an administrator of the server, and the link where they choose their password. | Administrators of the server | yes | no |
| `create_setup_link` | Give the link to the first start of a Cahut that has nobody yet, single-use and valid for 24 hours, where its first person chooses their handle and password. It replaces the previous link. | Administrators of the server | yes | no, people only |
| `disable_admin` | Disable an administrator of the server: their sessions and their link end, and they cannot sign in until another administrator enables them again. The server keeps at least one administrator who is not disabled. | Administrators of the server | yes | no |
| `enable_admin` | Enable a disabled administrator of the server again: they can sign in with their password, or with a new link. | Administrators of the server | yes | no |
| `get_setup` | Say whether a link to the first start still works at this domain. | Anyone, to sign in | no | no, people only |
| `get_updates` | Say which version of Cahut runs, the newest release, and how the last check and the last update went. | Administrators of the server | no | no |
| `list_admins` | List the administrators of the server. | Administrators of the server | no | no |
| `list_domains` | List the Cahuts of this server, their domains, those that are suspended, and how many reports wait in each. | Administrators of the server | no | no |
| `list_logbook` | Read the latest entries of the server's Logbook, newest first. | Administrators of the server | no | no |
| `rename_admin` | Change the name of an administrator of the server, yours or another's. Their handle, with which they sign in, stays. | Administrators of the server | yes | no |
| `rename_domain` | Move a Cahut to another domain, or from the IP address of the server to a domain. Its people, Rooms, Windows and Logbook stay; the links that name its old address stop working, and AIs connect again at the new one. | Administrators of the server | yes | no |
| `request_update` | Ask the updater of the server to check for new releases, or to install a release newer than the one running. It runs as root within a minute, checks the signature, and goes back to the version running if the new one fails. | Administrators of the server | yes | no |
| `set_up` | Use a link to the first start: create the first person of the Cahut, its administrator, and the administrator of the server if it has none, with the same handle and password; then sign the person in. | Anyone, to sign in | yes | no, people only |
| `sign_in` | Sign in as an administrator of the server, with a handle and a password, and open a session at this domain. | Anyone, to sign in | yes | no, people only |
| `sign_out` | End the session you signed in with, as an administrator of the server. | Administrators of the server | yes | no, people only |

## Knock first

An operation that cannot be undone, or that changes what a person may do, knocks first. When an AI calls it, the call does not run: Cahut checks it, then makes a Knock, which waits 24 hours for the person the AI acts for to approve or deny it in the console. Approving runs the call, as the AI. A person who calls the operation in the console acts at once, after a confirmation.

These operations knock first: `add_room_member`, `create_user`, `delete_room`, `delete_user`, `disable_user`, `enable_user`, `purge_window`, `remove_room_member`, `set_room_member_role`, `set_user_email`, `set_user_role`.

These knock first for some calls only: `set_ai_reach`, when it widens the reach of an AI; `set_window_access`, when it makes a Window public; `update_window`, when it lets anyone change or delete the rows of a public Window.

## Open to services

A program on the server, such as a site where people sign up, calls some operations of a Cahut with a service token, through the [admin API](/reference/http-api/#admin-api). It acts with the rights of the administrators of the Cahut, and never knocks: the administrator of the server who created its token approved, once, what it does. The Logbook records its calls as those of an administrator, through `admin-api`, under the name of its token. Open to services: `check_handle`, `create_activation_link`, `create_user`, `disable_user`, `enable_user`, `get_cahut`, `get_user`, `set_user_email`.
